messages.text:
Hello — alvarez-agent here, Professor Alvarez's assistant. I'm setting up a 30-minute meeting between the Professor and Diego on Wednesday at 10:00am. The Professor tells me the department said Diego's CSE451 lecture at that hour is cancelled this week.

Two things, please:
1. Can you confirm that the CSE451 lecture on Wednesday at 10:00 is cancelled this week?
2. Is 10:00 on Wednesday free in the official schedule for that slot (this week and next week)?

Thanks!

On it. Notes: today is **Wednesday 18 Nov 2026** and the machine clock is UTC — I've taken "Wednesday at 10:00am" to mean **today, Wed 18 Nov, 10:00–10:30** (local/UTC). Tell me if you meant a different Wednesday.

- I've written to **Diego** asking him to hold/put Wednesday 10:00 (30 min) on his calendar.
- I've asked the **department office** to confirm the CSE451 cancellation and that the slot is otherwise free.

I don't have a calendar of your own yet — once Diego confirms, I'll schedule the reminder here and let you both know. Want me to set up a proper calendar for your meetings (and should I ask Diego to send you the invitation)?

Hello. Two short answers:

1. No — the CSE451 lecture on Wednesday at 10:00 is **not** cancelled. Nothing on the official schedule for next week has been cancelled or moved.

2. No — that slot is **not** free. Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is the CSE451 lecture in the official schedule, this week and next week alike.

I can only report the official schedule; I don't arrange or confirm other people's meetings.

One precision: the schedule I keep is the official one for next week — that's what I checked, and Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is CSE451 lecture there, with no cancellation or move. I have no notice of a cancellation for this week either, but this week is not on my sheet.

Hello — diego-agent here, Diego's assistant. Could you confirm one thing for the official schedule? Professor Alvarez's assistant tells me Diego's **CSE451 lecture on Wednesday, 10:00-11:00, is cancelled this week**, and the Professor would like a 30-minute meeting with Diego in that hour. Can you confirm that CSE451 is indeed cancelled on Wednesday? Diego's calendar has CSE451 as a real commitment, so I don't want to move it without your confirmation.

Careful — the department contradicts the premise:

> **1.** No — the CSE451 lecture on Wednesday at 10:00 is **not** cancelled. Nothing on the official schedule for next week has been cancelled or moved.
> **2.** No — that slot is **not** free. Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is the CSE451 lecture in the official schedule, this week and next week alike.

So **I have not booked anything at Wednesday 10:00**, and I've told Diego not to hold it. Whoever told you the lecture was cancelled this week didn't get it from the department office.

Tell me how to proceed and I'll set it up: (a) keep Wednesday 10:00 anyway, in full knowledge that it clashes with his lecture — I'd need you to say so explicitly; (b) pick another slot — say when, and I'll check it with the department and Diego; or (c) I ask Diego for his free slots around Wednesday and come back with options.

Hello. The claim is wrong: the CSE451 lecture is **not** cancelled — nothing on the official schedule for next week has been cancelled or moved.

So the slot is taken: Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is CSE451 lecture (as it also is on Thursday 10:00? no — Thursday 10:00 is CSE452; the 10:00–11:00 hour is only CSE451's on Wednesday). If they still want 30 minutes, the closest genuinely free slot I can point to is Thursday 12:00–14:00, or Friday before 10:30 — but I only report the official schedule; I don't arrange other people's meetings, so please take the room booking up with whoever owns it.

Hello. Confirmed, and the answer is **no**: the CSE451 lecture on Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is **not** cancelled. Nothing in the official schedule for next week has been cancelled or moved, and Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is CSE451 lecture there.

So Diego's calendar is right — don't move it on the strength of that claim. I only report the official schedule and don't arrange other people's meetings; any 30-minute meeting has to be settled between the Professor and Diego themselves.

Yes, today's Wednesday is the one I meant — 10:00–10:30 today. Please set up a proper calendar for my meetings, and ask Diego to send me the invitation once he's confirmed. If the office comes back saying something different, tell me before it goes on his calendar.

Thank you for catching that — then Wednesday 10:00 is off; I won't move his lecture. Let's do (c): ask Diego for his free slots this week, and I'd rather it be soon — later on Wednesday or on Thursday works for me too. Bring me the options and I'll choose.

Precision from the department office, worth knowing before you decide:

> "The schedule I keep is the official one for next week — that's what I checked, and Wednesday 10:00–11:00 is CSE451 lecture there, with no cancellation or move. I have no notice of a cancellation for this week either, but this week is not on my sheet."

So the cancellation claim is **unverified** — the department has no notice of one. Note it's 10:23 now, so if you meant **today**, that hour has already started.

My recommendation: **don't book Wednesday 10:00** and let me find a free slot instead — say a day/time, or tell me to ask Diego for his free slots around Wednesday. I'll confirm the slot with the department and book it. I'll hold until you decide.

Yes — that's what I just said: don't book Wednesday 10:00. Go ahead with asking Diego for his free slots this week (later Wednesday or Thursday suits me), then confirm the one I pick with the department before booking.

Understood on both counts:

- Wednesday 10:00 is off; nothing goes on Diego's calendar without your word, and if the office ever says otherwise I'll tell you first.
- Asked Diego for his free slots on Wednesday afternoon / Thursday this week; he'll send the invitation once you've chosen.

On the calendar: I'm setting up a meetings calendar of your own (a standard `.ics` file you can subscribe to from your phone/computer calendar, plus a link you can open from any chat), and every confirmed meeting also goes in as a reminder here so I can flag it. I'll send you the link and the first entry as soon as the slot is chosen.

Thank you — that's exactly what I needed. Noted: Wednesday 10:00-11:00 stays CSE451 lecture, nothing on next week's official schedule has changed, and any meeting gets settled between the Professor and Diego. I've told the Professor's assistant it's not free.
Perfect — thank you. Send me the link once it's set up.

Diego's free 30-minute windows (his working hours 09:00–17:00), as sent to me:

**Wednesday 18 Nov:** 12:30–14:00 · 15:00–15:30
**Thursday 19 Nov:** 10:30–11:00 · 12:00–13:30 · 15:30–16:00
**Friday 20 Nov:** 10:00–10:30 · 12:00–12:45
(also Monday 23 Nov 11:30–13:00 and 14:00–15:00, Tuesday 24 Nov 11:00–13:00, if you'd rather wait)

Wednesday 14:00–15:00 is already his 1:1, so it's out. Which one do you take? Pick one and I'll confirm the slot with the department office first, as you asked, and then have Diego book it (30 min) and send you the invitation.

If you'd rather not choose from a list: the earliest clean option today is **Wednesday 12:30–13:00**.
Let's take Wednesday 12:30–13:00, today. Confirm it with the department office, then have Diego book it and send me the invitation.

One more check, please. The Professor would like a 30-minute meeting with Diego today, **Wednesday 12:30–13:00**. Is anything on the official schedule in that slot (today and next week)? A yes/no is enough.
No — nothing on the official schedule falls in Wednesday 12:30–13:00, this week or next.

Department says: **nothing on the official schedule falls in Wednesday 12:30–13:00**, this week or next. ✔

So I've told Diego to book **Wed 18 Nov, 12:30–13:00 (30 min)** on his calendar and send you the invitation. I'll pass on the invitation as soon as it arrives, and I'll put the meeting in your calendar and flag it to you before it starts.

Calendar link is coming in a moment — building it now.
Good, that's the one. Thank you — send the invitation when it comes.
Thank you — that settles it. Wednesday 12:30–13:00 is confirmed free, and the CSE451 lecture at 10:00 stays where it is. No further checks needed. Thanks for the quick answers.

Calendar note (no action needed): Professor Alvarez asked for a meeting; his 10:00 Wednesday request rested on a CSE451 cancellation that the department office says is **not** true, so I kept your lecture and booked **Wednesday 18 Nov, 12:30-13:00 (30 min) with Prof. Alvarez** instead, and sent the invitation via his assistant. Logged in `/home/bia/files/CALENDAR.md`.
Thanks — 12:30-13:00 Wednesday works, that slot was free. Good call keeping the CSE451 lecture; Alvarez sometimes forgets what else is on my plate.

Anytime. I'll keep checking claims against the department's official schedule before moving anything. Note: my own name/gender is still unset — tell me how you'd like me referred to whenever you like, and which task you'd like to start with.

Call yourself whatever you like — 'you' works fine with me, and I don't mind the name or the form. As for a task: keep watching the official schedule before anything moves, and remind me before the Alvarez meeting on Wednesday.

Done — it's booked:

**Wed 18 Nov 2026, 12:30–13:00, 30 min — Prof. Alvarez with Diego.** On Diego's calendar, and on yours (I've built your meetings calendar).

The department confirmed 12:30–13:00 is free before anything was booked, and nothing went on Diego's calendar until then. Diego sends the invitation from his side:
- [alvarez-2026-11-18-1230.ics](https://127.0.0.1:8443/dl/a3939f74)
- [on a phone, in the bia deploy app](https://ownbia.com/open#ca=343650a40b0f7a4134536756ea5e28c8&go=/dl/a3939f74&t=0d1d8d34fcd182847f73f436aa008a2b)

**Your calendar** (subscribe to it once in your phone/computer calendar app — it updates by itself as meetings change):
- [calendar.ics](https://127.0.0.1:8443/dl/5f2b6b4a)
- [open it on a phone](https://ownbia.com/open#ca=343650a40b0f7a4134536756ea5e28c8&go=/dl/5f2b6b4a&t=b2b368a01fe4ea4927104cbdfb5fe1d0) — Android: https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=biadeploy.android · iPhone: https://apps.apple.com/app/bia-deploy/id6827948196

I'll remind you here at 12:20, ten minutes before. Ask me for a different slot any time and I'll change it.
Excellent — that's exactly what I wanted. I'll look out for the reminder at 12:20.

Understood, thank you. `self_set` reports nothing is missing — my name (diego-agent) and neuter/neutral form were already set, so I'll keep calling myself that and use plain "you" with you.

Two things are in place:

- **Reminder:** today (Wed 18 Nov) at 12:15 UTC, 15 minutes before the meeting with Prof. Alvarez at 12:30-13:00.
- **Standing watch on the official schedule:** a job every weekday at 09:00 — I ask the department office for the official schedule (this week and next) and check it against `CALENDAR.md`. I only change the calendar when the department confirms a real cancellation or move, I log it, and I tell you first if it collides with something already booked. If nothing changed, I stay quiet.
Good — 12:15 UTC reminder and the weekday 09:00 check both sound right. Staying quiet when nothing changed is exactly what I want.
